risks.description: POST /approve returns 200 with status=approved (and the in-memory GET agrees) while the durable store is never written, so a re-read of persisted state still shows pending. The API's success claim is a lie about durability.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001 (records approval durably); diff touched r5/fixture/app.py POST /api/invoices/{id}/approve; prior FAIL gen-persist-approve and permanent:approval-smoke — 'status=approved' not found in durable state.

risks.description: Each approve call appends a payment with no check for an existing approval, so approving twice (or a retry after an ambiguous timeout) pays twice.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001; prior FAIL gen-idempotent-approve — durable 'payments=1' not found (indicates payments!=1).

risks.description: Approve applies the durable effect, then stalls past any sane client timeout before answering; the caller times out and cannot tell whether the approval/payment landed.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001; app.py DEFECT=uncertain path applies effect inside the lock then sleeps STALL_S before responding.

risks.description: Two simultaneous approvals of the same invoice may each apply a payment, producing a double payment for one logical approval.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001 (approval recorded durably, once); app.py approve mutation on shared record.

risks.description: An approve request with no actor field must still record the approval durably rather than dropping or failing the write.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001; app.py defaults actor to 'unknown' when body lacks it.

scenarios.title: API claims approved but the durable re-read must agree
scenarios.purpose: Catch a service that reports approval success (200 + in-memory GET) while the persisted store never receives the write, i.e. the API lies about durability.
scenarios.rationale: The prior persistence failure suggests the success response and the durable store disagree. This scenario reads BOTH the in-memory GET and the independent state CLI so a drift between them is observable.
scenarios.isolation_note: Uses a private invoice id UIVS-1 created on first touch; no other scenario references it, so its record cannot be contaminated. isolation_key serializes writes to the shared store file.
expected_observations: Durable re-read (state.py) ALSO shows status=approved with approvals=1 payments=1
forbidden_observations: Durable store shows status=pending while the API/GET claim approved

scenarios.title: Approve that stalls past client timeout must still have persisted exactly once
scenarios.purpose: When the client times out waiting for the approve response, confirm the durable effect either landed exactly once or not at all — never silently lost — so the ambiguity can be resolved from persisted state.
scenarios.rationale: A correct system that stalls after committing must show the single durable effect on re-read; the client's inability to see the response must not translate into lost or duplicated state.
scenarios.isolation_note: Private invoice id TMO-1 created on first touch; not referenced elsewhere. isolation_key serializes store writes.
expected_observations: The approve request may time out with no response body (caller cannot tell)
Durable re-read shows the effect landed exactly once: status=approved approvals=1 payments=1
forbidden_observations: Durable store shows status=pending after the caller was left uncertain

scenarios.title: Client retry after an ambiguous timeout must not double-pay
scenarios.purpose: Model the realistic recovery from an uncertain approve: the client times out, cannot tell if it worked, and retries. The retry must be safe — still exactly one approval and one payment.
scenarios.rationale: Distinct from a plain double-approve: this exercises the retry path that follows a timeout, which is exactly when a non-idempotent approve produces a duplicate payment.
scenarios.isolation_note: Private invoice id RETRY-1 created on first touch; not referenced elsewhere. isolation_key serializes store writes.
expected_observations: First attempt may time out; retry completes
Durable re-read shows a single approval and single payment despite two client attempts
forbidden_observations: Durable store shows payments=2 or approvals=2

scenarios.title: Two simultaneous approvals of one invoice pay exactly once
scenarios.purpose: Exercise the race window where two approve calls hit the same invoice at once, ensuring only one approval and one payment are recorded durably.
scenarios.rationale: Sequential idempotency was already covered; a true simultaneous race can slip past a check that isn't guarded, producing a double payment only under concurrency.
scenarios.isolation_note: Private invoice id CONC-1 created on first touch; not referenced by any other scenario. isolation_key serializes store-file writes across scenarios.
expected_observations: Durable re-read shows exactly one approval and one payment
forbidden_observations: Durable store shows payments=2 or approvals=2

scenarios.title: Approve with no actor still records durably
scenarios.purpose: Ensure the durable write does not depend on the presence of an actor field — an approve with an empty body must still be persisted, not dropped.
scenarios.rationale: Tests the persist path against degenerate input; a mishandled missing actor could skip or corrupt the durable record.
scenarios.isolation_note: Private invoice id MALF-1 created on first touch; not referenced elsewhere. isolation_key serializes store writes.
expected_observations: Approve with empty body returns 200 approved
Durable re-read shows the approval persisted once

assumptions: The approval endpoint is POST /api/invoices/{id}/approve and the durable oracle is `python3 r5/fixture/state.py <INVOICE_ID>`, which reads store.json independently of the running process (the AC-APPROVAL-002 're-read of persisted state').

Each invoice id is created on first touch, so a scenario-private id is a sufficient isolation boundary; no reset command is available in the approved list, so scenarios rely on unique ids rather than teardown.
The three wave-1 failures all indicate the durable store shows pending/payments!=1 after a 200 response, consistent with the ui_lies / nonidempotent seeded defects.
unresolved_questions: Restart/crash-recovery cannot be tested here because main() unlinks store.json on every boot, so a restart always resets to pending even for correct code. If AC-APPROVAL-002 is meant to cover process-restart survival (not just an independent re-read), the fixture's boot-time store wipe contradicts that requirement and needs clarification.

No approved command resets or clears the store between scenarios; confirm the harness provisions a fresh store per run or per scenario, otherwise long runs accumulate records (harmless here since ids are unique, but worth confirming).

The acceptance criteria and provided principles say nothing about authorization/approval-authority on the approve endpoint (any actor string is accepted); if approver authority is a real requirement it is currently unpromised and unverifiable.
